record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: How should one explain the apparently universal second term in the asymptotic expansion of the mutual energy of the zero counting measure and the measure |p_n|^2 w(x) dx for orthogonal polynomials? In particular, is the constant 1/2 the logarithmic capacity of the support, is there a direct proof not using the entropy identity, and does the same second-term asymptotic persist for a larger class of weights?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 5.5. What is the explanation of this “universal” behavior of the second term? Is the constant 1/2 appearing there the logarithmic capacity of the support of the measure of orthogonality? Is there any direct proof of (5.3) which does not use (5.2)? Is (5.3) still valid in a larger class of weights w?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w$ be a non-negative weight function on a compact set $E\subset\mathbb{R}$ (with $w>0$ a.e. on $E$ and sufficiently regular, e.g., satisfying the Szegő/Erdős-class conditions on $[-1,1]$), and let $\{p_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be the sequence of polynomials orthonormal with respect to $w(x)\,dx$ on $E$. For each $n$, let 
$$\nu_n=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\delta_{x_{j,n}}$$
denote the normalized zero-counting measure of $p_n$, and let $\mu_n$ denote the probability measure $|p_n(x)|^2 w(x)\,dx$ on $E$. Define the mutual logarithmic energy
$$I(\nu_n,\mu_n)=\iint \log\frac{1}{|x-y|}\,d\nu_n(x)\,d\mu_n(y).$$
It is known that, for the classical setting, an asymptotic expansion of the form
$$I(\nu_n,\mu_n)=A\log n+\tfrac12\cdot\frac{\log n}{n}+o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)$$
(or the analogous "universal" second-order term with constant $1/2$) appears, derived via an entropy identity relating $I(\nu_n,\mu_n)$ to the logarithmic energy of $\nu_n$ and the entropy of $\mu_n$.

Provide a conceptual explanation of this universal second-order term. In particular:
(i) Determine whether the constant $1/2$ appearing in the second term equals the logarithmic capacity of the support of the orthogonality measure, or identify what quantity it represents.
(ii) Give a direct proof of the second-order asymptotic that does not pass through the entropy identity.
(iii) Determine the largest natural class of weights $w$ for which the same second-order asymptotic remains valid.
artifact.category_tag: orthogonal polynomials and logarithmic potential theory
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution explaining the universal $1/2$ second-term constant in the mutual-energy asymptotics or providing a direct (non-entropy) proof, nor a definitive extension to a broader weight class. Related work on strong asymptotics, equilibrium measures, and entropy of orthogonal polynomials is abundant, but no source directly answering these three questions was identified.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal Polynomials (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses zero distributions and entropy/energy identities for orthogonal polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the entropy identity used to derive the second-term asymptotic, with no resolution of the universal constant question.

status_evidence.title: The asymptotic zero distribution of orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Studies weak convergence of zero counting measures to equilibrium measures via logarithmic potential theory.
status_evidence.claim: Relevant background, but does not address the explicit second-order $1/2$ constant problem.
